newsitem.title: CUBA: Quiet emotion marks return of Che Guevara's remains.
newsitem.headline: Quiet emotion marks return of Che Guevara's remains.

text.p: A brief, quietly emotional ceremony marked the return to Cuba of the remains of legendary revolutionary Ernesto "Che" Guevara, 30 years after he was captured and shot while leading a guerrilla uprising in Bolivia.

The remains, unearthed last week from a secret mass grave near Vallegrande, Bolivia, were flown to the military airbase of San Antonio de los Banos near Havana late on Saturday and received by President Fidel Castro, members of Guevara's family, and old comrades-in-arms.
The ceremony, a military tribute to one of Cuba's most revered heroes, was broadcast to ordinary Cubans shortly before midnight (0400 GMT) on state radio and television.

Guevara's daughter Aleida Guevara March, her voice breaking slightly with emotion, read an address to Castro on behalf of the children of Guevara and of three Cuban guerrilla comrades whose remains were exhumed from the same mass grave in Bolivia and also returned to Cuba on Saturday.
"Today their remains return to us, but they do not return vanquished, they come as heroes, always young, valiant, strong and brave," she said.

"It was more than 30 years ago that our fathers bade us farewell, they left to continue the ideas of (Simon) Bolivar and (Jose) Marti: a united and independent continent, but they did not manage to see this triumph," Aleida Guevara added.
"They were conscious that great dreams only become true with tremendous sacrifices. We never saw them again."
Guevara's closest surviving family are his Cuban widow Aleida March and his children Aleida, Camilo, Celia and Ernesto. It was at their request that Saturday's ceremony was brief and sombre.
Guevara, an Argentine doctor, was Castro's right-hand man in the guerrilla struggle that led to the overthrow of Cuban dictator Fulgencio Batista in January 1959.

Guevara left Cuba in the mid-1960s to continue fighting for his revolutionary ideals, first in Africa and then in Bolivia, where he was killed by Bolivian troops in October 1967. He became an icon for a generation of leftists around the world and is still revered in Cuba.

His remains were taken to the Armed Forces (Defense) Ministry in Havana's Revolution Square. In October, they will be moved to a mausoleum being specially built in the square that bears his name in the central town of Santa Clara.
Santa Clara was the site of a decisive battle led by Guevara in December 1958 against Batista's army.
